descriptions.value: littlefs 2.8.0 through 2.11.3 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability in lfs_mount_() that allows attackers to crash processes mounting crafted filesystem images when block_count is 0. Attackers can supply an image lacking a superblock entry or recording block_count 0, causing lfs->seed % lfs->block_count to trigger SIGFPE and denial of service.

Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic (Cypher injection) in the fulltext and vector index query generator of the sharded property database in Neo4j Enterprise Edition 2026.07.0 before 2026.10.0 allows an authenticated user holding ACCESS, CREATE INDEX and NAME MANAGEMENT privileges to inject Cypher that is accepted for execution on a property shard, in the session of any user who later queries the index, via a crafted index name containing a single quote. The impact is bounded by the privileges of the querying user.
Use of uninitialized memory when processing certain font files in X.Org libXfont before 2.0.10 could be used by authenticated attackers to crash the X server.

Mattermost Plugins versions <=12.-1 11.0.11 11.11.7 11.2.10.0 fail to check for a nil result after decoding the HTTP request body which allows an authenticated user to crash the Zoom plugin process, causing denial of service, via sending a JSON null body to the plugin's action endpoints. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00722

Mattermost Plugins versions <=12.-1 11.0.11 11.11.7 11.2.10.0 fail to verify that the caller can post in a run's channel when executing a checklist slash command which allows an authenticated run participant to post arbitrary messages into a private channel they are not a member of via the checklist item run endpoint. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00730

Mattermost Plugins versions <=12.-1 11.11.7 11.2.10 11.1.11.0 fail to enforce the GitLab project permission check for confidential issues when the project is publicly visible which allows an authenticated user with no GitLab membership in the project to obtain the contents of confidential issues, including title, description, author, and URL via subscribing a channel to the parent public GitLab group with the confidential_issues feature and waiting for a confidential issue webhook event. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00738

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP GetConfiguration Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP messages. When parsing GetConfiguration requests, the process does not properly validate the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28968.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A Wi-Fi Configuration Server Missing Authentication Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to modify Wi-Fi configuration on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of Wi-Fi configuration requests. The issue results from the lack of authentication prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29068.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP backend configuration requests. The issue results from the lack of authentication prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29063.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A Download of Code Without Integrity Check Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP messages. The issue results from the lack of proper verification of firmware integrity prior to installation. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28957.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Hard-Coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the configuration of the OCPP backend settings interface. The issue results from the use of hard-coded credentials. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29056.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A FTP URL Path Parsing Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of FTP URL paths during firmware updates. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28960.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP UpdateFirmware Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP UpdateFirmware requests. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a write past the end of an allocated buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29487.

A flaw was found in Moodle. The grade feedback web service does not properly verify group and course enrolment permissions. An authenticated user with non-editing teacher privileges can exploit this vulnerability to access grade feedback and user profile details across groups or courses they are not authorized to view, leading to unauthorized information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Moodle's Blackboard question import format. Insufficient validation of file paths during the question import process allows an authenticated user with permissions to import questions into a question bank to read arbitrary files accessible to the web server process. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to view sensitive files, resulting in unauthorized information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing capability check in the grade items web service, an authenticated user with a student role can view the names of all grade items in a course, including those intended to be hidden. This flaw leads to unauthorized information disclosure of hidden course assessment details.

A flaw was found in Moodle's external database enrolment plugin. Insufficient sanitization of data passed to queries against the external database allows an authenticated user with course editing permissions to perform a Structured Query Language (SQL) injection attack. When this non-default plugin is enabled, an attacker can exploit this issue to view, modify, or delete sensitive records within the connected external database.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient validation when saving activity settings, an authenticated user with teacher privileges can modify activities in courses they are not authorized to access. This flaw allows unauthorized changes to course materials, compromising the integrity of course content.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient sanitization of objective identifiers in the SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model) objectives report allows an authenticated user with content upload permissions to inject malicious scripts. When another user views the report, the injected script executes in their browser session, potentially allowing the attacker to access sensitive information or perform unauthorized actions on their behalf.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient permission checks and input validation in the quiz question bank callback, an authenticated user can access and view questions from question banks they do not have permission to access. Furthermore, this issue allows users to trigger arbitrary class instantiation (creating unintended application objects), potentially leading to further unauthorized actions.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Missing ownership verification in Feedback activity templates allows an authenticated teacher to view, use, or delete templates associated with courses other than their own. This can result in unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of course materials.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to missing ownership checks in badge alignments, an authenticated user with badge management privileges can view and modify alignments associated with badges they do not own. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data disclosure and tampering with badge configurations.

A flaw was found in Moodle. An improper authorization check when displaying individual glossary entries allows an authenticated user to view approved glossary items from courses they do not have permission to access. This vulnerability leads to unauthorized information disclosure of restricted educational materials.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Missing authorization checks in the forum discussion web services allow authenticated users to view discussion information in courses they do not have permission to access. In addition, users with teacher privileges may lock forum discussions in courses where they lack proper authorization. This issue can lead to unauthorized information disclosure and unauthorized discussion state modification.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing authorization check when viewing and restoring wiki page versions, an authenticated user can access content from courses they are not permitted to view. This issue allows an attacker to inspect restricted course material and copy it into their own wiki pages, leading to unauthorized information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing authorization check when editing Lesson activity pages, authenticated users with teacher privileges can view and move lesson pages from courses they are not permitted to access into their own lessons. This issue can lead to unauthorized access and modification of restricted course content.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient authorization checks in the quiz editing functionality allow an authenticated user with teacher privileges to view slot details and modify sections of quizzes they do not have permission to manage. An attacker could exploit this flaw to alter quiz configurations or disclose quiz structure information without proper authorization.

A flaw was found in Moodle's single view grade report web service. A missing authorization check allows authenticated students to view the names of all grade items in a course, including those configured to be hidden. This vulnerability leads to unauthorized information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient authorization checks in the quiz overrides web service allow an authenticated user with teacher privileges to modify user and group overrides for quizzes they do not have permission to manage. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to improperly alter exam access, deadlines, or testing conditions across unauthorized courses.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient authorization checks in the quiz random question filter web service, an authenticated user with teacher privileges can modify random question settings in quizzes they do not have permission to manage. This flaw allows unauthorized users to alter assessment configurations across courses they do not oversee.

Quasar before 2.35.3 contains a DOM clobbering vulnerability that allows attackers to break native wrapper detection by injecting HTML elements named Capacitor, cordova, or StatusBar. Attackers can place markup such as a div with id Capacitor into server-rendered or pre-rendered HTML so app.use(Quasar) throws and the application never mounts, or openURL() and AddressbarColor.set() throw.

Stoatchat before 0.16.5 contains an unbounded JXL image decoding vulnerability in revolt_files decode_image that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory via the january /proxy endpoint. Attackers can request a small hosted JXL file declaring 12000x12000 pixels through /proxy to trigger huge allocations, OOM-killing january and denying proxy and embed service.

Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows space admins to reach internal hosts because Nextcloud.get_client builds WebDAV clients from Storage.url without calling safe_request. Attackers can create a NEXTCLOUD storage via POST /api/storage/ pointing at internal hosts, import a file, then call GET /api/get_recipe_file/<id>/ to read internal service or cloud metadata responses.

Modoboa before 2.13.0 contains a CRLF injection vulnerability that allows Resellers or users with domain add or change permission to inject rspamd DKIM selector map entries by supplying an unvalidated dkim_key_selector through the relay domain API. Attackers can embed a carriage return in the selector to override another tenant's domain selector, causing rspamd to sign its outgoing mail with a nonexistent selector and fail DKIM verification.

Manyfold 0.124.0 before 0.154.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to make the instance fetch internal URLs by supplying malicious ActivityPub actor icon.url and image.url fields. Attackers can deliver Create or Update activities to the inbox, causing the Shrine remote_url plugin to request internal or cloud metadata hosts and store responses as creator avatar or banner attachments.

SABnzbd before 5.2.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the Sorter that allows attackers to write files outside the Complete folder via crafted propername, episodename or job name (%dn) values. Attackers can supply a malicious NZB with '...' sequences that collapse to '..' after single-pass replacement, moving downloaded files into arbitrary directories writable by SABnzbd.

OpnForm before 2.8.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to move other forms' shared assets by supplying their URLs in file upload fields. Attackers can submit a public form with another form's cover or logo URL, causing Storage::move() to relocate it into submissions and break that asset.

OpnForm before 2.8.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in PublicWebhookUrl::isPublicIp that fails to reject CGNAT, NAT64 and 6to4 address ranges. Authenticated users can configure webhook, form import or PDF image URLs resolving to these ranges to make the server send HTTPS requests to internal hosts.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject iframe attributes via the maxheight parameter of the GET /oembed endpoint. Attackers can supply a single quote in maxheight to inject an onload handler into the returned html, executing script in third-party oEmbed consumers that embed it unsanitized.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by crafting og:video:secure_url values. Attackers can post links to pages whose allowlisted-prefix video URL contains a quote and onload handler, executing script in readers' sessions when they click the video preview.

node-soap before 1.14.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in WSDL.xmlToObject that allows unauthenticated attackers to pollute Object.prototype via an XML element with id="__proto__". Attackers can send a single crafted SOAP request to a soap.listen() server, or return a malicious response to a client, causing all subsequent SOAP parsing to fail until process restart.

parse5-html-rewriting-stream 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in RewritingStream#emitText, which skips escaping based on a stale lastStartTagName. Attackers can place entity-encoded markup after a closed script or style element to bypass RewritingStream-based filters and execute script in users' browsers.

parse5 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability in Preprocessor#_processSurrogate that allows remote attackers to crash applications by supplying two consecutive low surrogates. Attackers can submit input such as U+DC00 U+DC00, which decodes to out-of-range code point 0x110000 and throws a RangeError from parse, parseFragment, or streaming parsers, crashing Node.js processes.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a local file inclusion vulnerability that allows administrators to include arbitrary server files by storing ../ sequences in the content manager file name. Unauthenticated requests to shop_content.php then pass the stored path to include(), executing embedded PHP in uploaded content files or images as the web server user.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in admin/support.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via the module parameter. Attackers can trick a logged-in administrator into opening a crafted link to run script in the admin panel, reading CSRF tokens and changing shop settings.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows administrators with product editing permission to inject script via the products_name field. The unescaped name is rendered in the h1 heading of product detail and reviews pages, executing script in the browsers of shoppers and logged-in customers.
In JetBrains Datalore before 2026.4.1 improper authorization allowed notebook viewers to read attached environment variable values
In JetBrains Datalore before 2026.4.1 open redirect after OpenID login was possible via the origin parameter
In JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA before 2026.3 untrusted projects could read files of other open projects via the built-in web server
In JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA before 2026.3, 2026.2.4 code execution was possible in untrusted projects via the Code Provenance plugin
